#1695. GdS: Super in Serie A, struggling in Europe – the reasons behind the ‘two-faced’ Milan

AC Milan are having a positive start to the 2026-27 season in Serie A, but in the Europa League they have been poor. Why exactly is that the case?

Milan go into tonight’s game against Olympiacos needing a win in order to start putting things right in a competition in which they have so far lost three out of four. The top eight expectation has now vanished, with even a play-off spot in jeopardy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Amorim has been coaching two teams since the summer: one which is excellent in the league with some ups and downs, and another that is frankly terrible when the Europa League anthem players.

Milan score 2.33 goals per game in the league on average, compared to just 1 per game in Europe. All four of those goals in the UEL came in the win over RB Salzburg too: they have drawn a blank in the other three.

Looking a bit deeper, Milan have less possession in Europa League matches (53%, compared to 59% in the league) but shoot 12.5 times per game, more than in Serie A. In Europe they get into the box more often: 26 touches in the opponent’s box compared to 23.

So, why do they score so much less despite being more threatening? Simply put, they shoot worse: the Rossoneri have a very high conversion rate in Serie A (26.4%) which plummets to 10% in Europe. This means that in the UEL it takes 10 shots to score a goal, while in the league it only takes four.

It’s not all mathematics. Anyone who has watched Milan in Europe have noticed their difficulties. At Bournemouth, they were never in the game, against Ferencvaros they collapsed, against Benfica they deserved to lose against a fellow contender.

With just hours to go before the match against the best defence in the competition, another test awaits. However, Amorim must find a way to concede less too. In Europe, Milan concede 1.92 xG per game, while in the league it’s just 1.28.

This all leads to a discussion about line-ups, and Amorim has rotated a lot outside of league action. The right defender has always been Filippo Terracciano or Fikayo Tomori, never Mario Gila. Without the Spaniard, there’s a noticeable difference.

In midfield, Luka Modric has never started, and Adrien Rabiot started only against Salzburg and Ferencvaros. Up front, Diego Moreira started only against Bournemouth. Life, with or without those three, changes completely.

Amorim already knows he won’t have Modric against Olympiacos, but he can plan with Rabiot and Moreira, concocting a strong side despite the injury issues. He’ll ask for overtime tonight and on Monday in Cagliari, knowing his side will then have almost a week to rest.

#1694. Mikel Arteta drops new William Saliba return hint with Arsenal star ‘desperate’ to play

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba is set to make his first-team return for Arsenal in the upcoming matches.

The Frenchman missed the first three months of the season with a back injury that he aggravated at the World Cup in the summer.

Although surgery was not needed, Saliba still required a lengthy period of rest and he is yet to play a single competitive minute for Mikel Arteta’s senior side this season.

He has, however, featured in a couple of behind-closed-doors friendly matches at Arsenal’s training ground. Saliba also played 45 minutes for the Under-21s before the recent international break.

The centre-back was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund but remained an unused substitute on each occasion.

Arsenal have a relentless run of fixtures coming up before Christmas, including several huge matches. The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday as they look to put a nine-point gap between the two clubs in the Premier League title race.

Arteta indicated that Saliba is unlikely to be thrown straight into the starting lineup against City, but could expect to feature very soon.

“Obviously he hasn’t played football for a long, long time,” Arteta said at his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“He can play a certain amount of minutes, so we need to be really, really sure. Especially in that kind of game when he comes in, that he can sustain a certain amount of minutes otherwise we’re not going to have enough subs or opportunities to make those subs.

“He’s training well, he will have minutes in the next few games. Then he will prove what he’s already done, which is that he’s an unbelievable player.”

Asked how many minutes Saliba was now capable of playing, Arteta added: “Now he’s got more training, another week or 10 days, that will extend.

“It will depend as well on the type of game and the exposure that he will have throughout the game.”

#1693. Ipswich Town vs. Aston Villa: Unai Emery's side bidding to extend 42-year streak in Portman Road fixture

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 12:29

Aston Villa will be bidding to extend a 42-year streak when they face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening.

Unai Emery's side make the trip to Portman Road sitting in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

Furthermore, Villa are currently on a six-match winless streak, leading to Sports Mole arguing that Emery is no longer untouchable at the West Midlands outfit.

However, with a run of Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace to come in England's top flight, Emery will be optimistic that his team can turn around their fortunes.

Furthermore, Villa make the long trip to East Anglia looking to prolong a streak that has lasted more than four decades.

When the teams met in the 2024-25 Premier League campaign, they played out draws at their respective grounds.

Nevertheless, Villa earning a 2-2 draw on their travels extended their unbeaten streak at Portman Road to 10 matches.

Not since September 1984 have they suffered defeat at the home of the Tractor Boys, while Ipswich have incredibly only prevailed twice since that occasion.

That said, Ipswich have recorded draws in four of their last five home games against Villa, their only defeat coming in the 2017-18 Championship when they lost by a 4-0 scoreline.

Neither side has scored more than two goals in the last four head-to-heads, nor have they kept a clean sheet.

Newly-promoted Ipswich can move ahead of Champions League participants Villa this weekend.

If Gary O'Neil's side prevail by at least a two-goal margin, they will move ahead of Villa in the Premier League standings.

While Ipswich have collected seven points from five home fixtures, Villa have accumulated eight points from the same amount of away games.

However, neither team has won a game during November.

#1692. Renee Slegers: Arsenal confirm manager exit as statement issued

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Renee Slegers has left Arsenal by mutual consent after the club’s poor start to the Women’s Super League season.

The Gunners sit sixth in the table and are already 12 points off the pace set by Chelsea, having drawn all six of their league matches on home soil.

A goalless draw with West Ham last weekend has proved to be Slegers’ final match in charge.

Slegers took charge as interim head coach in October 2024 and was then given the permanent job three months later.

That season ended in glory for Arsenal, who won their second Champions League title in May 2025. Earlier this year, the club won the inaugural FIFA Women’s Champions Cup.

However, results have dipped significantly this season and Arsenal have used the international break to make the change in head coach, with Slegers’ assistant Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club.

“It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here,” said director of women’s football Clare Wheatley.

“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.

#1690. A tale of glory or misery in Greece: All the key stats ahead of Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan and Olympiacos will face each other for a fifth time this evening, with the Greek side hosting the Rossoneri in Athens.

The first two meetings came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19. In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent encounters were eight years ago, as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Milan have never won a competitive game against a Greek side in Greece, losing 2 and drawing 4. However, they have lifted the Champions League trophy twice in Athens (4-0 vs. Barcelona in 1994 and 2-1 vs. Liverpool in 2007).

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

#1689. The truth behind Manchester United triggering Bruno Fernandes contract extension

Manchester United had the January transfer window in mind when triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, but now run until the summer of 2028.

Fernandes confirmed last week that he had put contract negotiations with United on hold due to the club’s ongoing struggles on the pitch, having already rejected two offers of new terms.

Man Utd head into the Premier League weekend sitting in 19th place in the Premier League, and welcome sixth-placed Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday in what is new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

Fernandes has struggled to reproduce the form that earned him a host of individual awards last season, and Standard Sport understands that both parties believe it is sensible to return to negotiations at a later date.

But that left Fernandes open to approaches for foreign teams with pre-contract offers ahead of the summer.

To prevent any further distractions, Fernandes has been tied up for a further 12 months and will return to the negotiation table once the club are on more assured footing form-wise.

But an exit this summer can not yet be ruled out.

Fernandes may not be able to help his team-mates on Saturday, though, having been struck down by an illness which prevented him from training on Friday morning.

Confirming the issue later on Friday, Pochettino said of Fernandes: "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

The club captain was unable to train on Friday morning due to a virus, which has thrown into doubt his involvement in Pochettino’s first home match in charge.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, and this is a potentially huge spanner to throw into the works.

Fernandes’s absence could see Matheus Cunha move into the No10 role, supported by Amad Diallo and Patrick Dorgu, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Elsewhere, the new manager also has a decision to make in defence. Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, a more timid back three seems unlikely.

It will be a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game.

Brentford’s pace in behind may necessitate a quicker backline, meaning Maguire could make way again here, having also reportedly complained of an injury after the midweek match.

Lisandro Martinez has been at left-back, but Dorgu’s attacking qualities will likely be required on Saturday and Luke Shaw is also now back in training. By moving Martinez back to centre-half alongside Yoro, Pochettino can find the pace required. Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Pochettino has quickly settled on a midfield partnership of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans, who was controversially sent off late on against Sporting but is available in the Premier League.

Should Fernandes be passed fit, the attack continues to pick itself - if not their exact positions.

Fernandes was deployed on the left behind Cunha in the defeat by Liverpool, while Mbeumo was briefly used as the lone forward under Michael Carrick.

Here, we’re predicting Cunha to lead the line after his midweek rest due to suspension, with Fernandes in behind as the No10 and Mbeumo on the left wing.

If Amad is fit enough to start after being forced off in the draw with Sporting, expect the Ivorian on the right flank. If not, youngster Shea Lacey could be a candidate to start.

Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain injured, as do midfielders Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino revealed that Baleba would be out for 10 to 12 weeks from when he sustained his hamstring issue against Roma in early November.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Brentford (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Martinez, Dorgu; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha

#1687. Maher optimistic Nashville can turn MLS Cup playoff tie against Cincinnati around

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Nashville SC defender Jack Maher revealed he is "so confident" his team-mates can defeat FC Cincinnati in their MLS Cup playoff tie.

Nashville won the 2026 Supporters' Shield in stunning fashion, setting a new single-season points record (77), but made a losing start to the postseason.

BJ Callaghan's side lost Game 1 in Round One at home 1-0 after an early own goal from Patrick Yazbek, marking their first defeat at GEODIS Park in MLS play this season.

Nashville must now defeat Cincinnati in Game 2 on Saturday to keep the series alive, and Maher is optimistic they can get the job done at TQL Stadium.

"First loss at home in MLS play for the whole entire year, and I think that that's something that clearly is frustrating," said Maher.

"The mood around the locker room was that this hasn't really happened before this year. But we're optimistic about the next game, and we're going to give it clearly everything we got.

"It's a hungry group in that locker room, and I think that if [Cincinnati] want to go on, they got to beat us twice.

"I'm so confident that we have the guys in this locker room to be able to go up to Cincinnati, get a great result, come back home, and finish the job."

Nashville boss Callaghan added: "This team's battle-tested, and the group will be ready to respond.

"You can feel that there's a bit of a hunger. This team has continually showed that we have the experience from early in the season in playing knockout-type games, and the group will be prepared to respond."

Who's making the trip to Cincy? @Fly_Nashville https://t.co/mqje0Lc5FC

— Nashville SC (@NashvilleSC) November 24, 2026

Evander was held without a shot or a chance created in the Game 1 victory.

The match was Evander's 69th MLS game with Cincinnati (regular season and playoffs), but just the second time he finished without a single shot contribution (the other was against Atlanta United in the 2026 season opener).

Over his eight MLS seasons, Hany Mukhtar has scored 37 goals and added 28 assists on the road in MLS play (including playoffs).

His 65 away goal contributions make him one of two MLS players with at least 60 goal contributions on the road since 2020, along with Carles Gil (71).

After a tightly fought contest in Game 1, the Opta supercomputer has predicted a similar outcome in this encounter, which could be decided by penalties.

With a 1-0 win in Game 1, Cincinnati levelled the all-time series against Nashville at five wins apiece (D4) across all competitions. Sunday's win was just Cincinnati's second clean sheet ever against Nashville, joining another 1-0 road win (March 2023).

The winner was the second time this season Cincinnati benefited from an own goal (the final goal in a 3-3 draw at Chicago in April). The own goal in Game 1 was the first playoff own goal from outside the box over the last 20 seasons.

The Game 1 loss ended a 10-match unbeaten streak against MLS opponents for Nashville (W7 D3). They have not lost consecutive matches in MLS play since October 2025, when they dropped their regular-season finale and playoff opener, both to Inter Miami.

#1686. Hearts vs Celtic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 27 Nov 2026 12:38

Hearts welcome Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic to Tynecastle Park for a matchday 15 showdown on Sunday.

The hosts are fourth in the Scottish Premiership table with 23 points from 13 games, while the visitors are top of the standings with 34 points after 14 matches.

Hearts head into Sunday's match off the back of a disappointing run of results, having recorded just one win and suffered four defeats in their last five matches.

The sole victory came in their last Scottish Premiership outing, with the Jambos sensationally defeating Dundee 8-0, a result that continued a trend of high-scoring fixtures for Hearts this term.

Hearts have been one of the most entertaining teams to follow in the Scottish Premiership this season, scoring 34 goals - the most in the division - and conceding a significant 22 times.

The Jambos have been involved in several blockbuster encounters, including the 8-0 win against Dundee and a 5-0 triumph over St Mirren, although they have also been on the wrong end of such scorelines.

Wouter Vrancken's side have lost 5-2 to Falkirk and suffered a humiliating 7-1 defeat against upcoming opponents Celtic on matchday nine, leaving the Jambos eager to exact their revenge on Sunday.

Celtic, meanwhile, are among the highest scorers in the Scottish Premiership, with 32 goals scored, but also boast the best defensive record in the division, conceding only 11 times.

The Bhoys head into the weekend placed at the top of the table with 34 points from 14 league matches, although second-placed Rangers may have moved top of the table by the time of Sunday's kick-off.

Celtic, regardless of Rangers' result, will be eager to maintain or extend their lead at the top of the standings, leaving Martin O'Neill aiming for a 12th win in 15 league games.

The league leaders will travel to Tynecastle confident of claiming all three points, especially after their 7-1 victory earlier in the campaign and their recent return to winning ways after a challenging period between mid-September and early November.

Celtic managed just three wins, one draw and suffered six defeats during that time, but they have since bounced back with four straight victories ahead of this encounter with the Jambos.

Hearts are dealing with several injury issues, including Malachi Fagan-Walcott, Stephen Kingsley, Tomas Magnusson, Calvin Miller, Oisin McEntee, Harry Milne, Tom Renaud and Craig Halkett.

Despite their devastating late defeat to Monaco in midweek, an encouraging performance could prompt Vrancken to name an unchanged starting 11 on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Celtic are set to remain without the availability of Mika Baur and Alistair Johnston due to injury problems.

Camilo Duran's sensational scoring start as a Celtic player continued in midweek with another goal against Torreense, marking his 15th of the campaign, and the forward should start on Sunday.

Reus; Altena, McCart, Findlay; Kerjota, Gillies, Mendy, Borchgrevink; Kabore, Braga, Guendouz

Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Oxlade-Chamberlain; Hassan, McCowan, Jota; Duran

Celtic are the favourites given the stark contrast in the two teams' form heading into this match, leading us to expect a comfortable win for the away side.

#1685. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1684. Tottenham: Roberto De Zerbi confirms new Dejan Kulusevski plan ahead of Sunderland trip

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that Dejan Kulusevski is closing in on his first Tottenham start in more than a year and a half.

Kulusevski made an emotional return to fitness last month, coming off the bench for his first appearance in 526 days following a serious patella injury as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The Swedish playmaker has since seen his minutes managed, with cameo appearances against Chelsea, Crystal Palace and Leeds before the international break.

Kulusevski was subsequently called up to Sweden’s squad for their Nations League fixtures against Bosnia and Poland earlier this month, playing a combined 54 minutes for Graham Potter’s side.

Spurs remain cautious about risking Kulusevski. But the 26-year-old’s performances over the international break have now convinced De Zerbi that he is nearly ready to start for the first time since Spurs’ 2-0 defeat to Crystal Palace on May 11, 2025.

“Listen, I am thinking to start maybe not now, but I think we are very close to start the game. He is working well. I watched his games in the national team just to understand the physical condition,” De Zerbi said in his pre-Sunderland press conference on Friday afternoon.

“He played the first game as a winger and the second game as a No.10 and especially in the second game he played very well, but we have to be good to understand the right moment to put him on the pitch. I think medical staff, physical staff, they are working very well with him and we can’t lose any time, but we can’t take any risk because he is a special player for us.”

Spurs have paid extra attention this season to managing the minutes of players with a history of injuries, with Dominic Solanke, Destiny Udogie and James Maddison all having faced spells out of the side in a bid to minimise the risk of them suffering long-term issues.

Udogie returned to the starting lineup for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United as Spurs beat Ipswich 2-0 last weekend.

Solanke, meanwhile, made just his sixth league start of the season, getting on the scoresheet in the second-half to seal the three points.

Asked about the pair, De Zerbi admitted that while they were making progress, Udogie would need to remain under close supervision from the club’s medical staff over the next three to four weeks.

“They’re working well also this week, both,” De Zerbi continued.

“Dominic Solanke, I think, played very well in the last game against Ipswich, and also Udogie.

“I think we have to manage Udogie better than Solanke because Udogie needs to stay with the medical staff, focusing on him for another three, four weeks, and then if he goes over this four weeks, I think for him it’s not a problem.”

#1683. GdS: Milan join Serie A rivals in race for 13-goal Monza sensation Varela

AC Milan have positioned themselves as one of the contenders in the race to sign Gustavo Varela, according to a report.

If someone had told Varela in August that three months later he’d be on double figures for goals in Serie A (11, 13 all competitions), perhaps even he wouldn’t have believed it. As a result of his exploits, La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm many top clubs in Italy are watching him with growing interest.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Napoli were the first team to make a move, but Milan are also in the mix, as are Inter and Juventus. That’s not all: several teams in the Premier League are following him, and worries about Moise Kean’s condition have seen Como enter the picture too.

More specifically, Napoli want to offload Lorenzo Lucca and have already made contact with Varela’s entourage. However, they must first sell to reach the figures Monza wants. Juventus also need a striker, but Financial Fair Play requires Juventus them to make a sale too.

Como spent €40m on Kean this summer but risk having to return to the market due to the Italian’s long lay-off. Inter are also interested in Varela, but they don’t need to strengthen their attack immediately.

Milan are looking for more goals and have their eye on Nicolo Tresoldi, but Varela could become a worthy alternative, considering he’s already familiar with Serie A. Compared to the other domestic competitors, the price matters least to the Rossoneri.

After scoring a gorgeous back-heel goal against Fiorentina, Varela was asked about his future: “The backheel goal was pure instinct. It’s not something I try in training. A great cross came in, I was right there near the goal, and I decided to give it a try.

“I continue to thank Monza for letting me be here. It’s all been crazy so far: I feel very lucky to be part of this team, and I only hope it can continue like this. Transfer rumors are part of football. I’m having a great time right now, and I’m just trying to enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.”

Unfortunately for Varela this feels impossible, considering everyone’s talking about him at the moment, and will continue to while he is scoring goals at the rate he is.

#1682. Man City XI vs Arsenal: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after only 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose again in north London on Sunday.

City are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home across all competitions in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a potentially cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few games. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

Maresca revealed at his pre-match press conference on Friday that Antoine Semenyo was close to returning from a knee injury sustained against Ipswich last month, though the trip to Arsenal will come too soon for his comeback.

#1681. PEC Zwolle vs AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 27 Nov 2026 12:54, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:35

Two of the Eredivisie’s most in-form sides meet in round 14, as PEC Zwolle face AZ Alkmaar at the Mac3Park Stadion on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts are unbeaten in their last five league matches, while the visitors are seeking a fourth consecutive victory in all competitions.

After losing three consecutive matches for the first time in almost a year around the start of November, AZ Alkmaar have responded with three straight victories. Their most recent success was a 4-2 win over Sparta Prague in Thursday’s Europa League fixture.

Leeroy Echteld’s men had to come from behind again in their midweek victory at epet ARENA and have now conceded the opening goal in each of their last six matches, often leaving them chasing matches more than they would ideally like.

Having scored 13 goals during their current winning run, De Kaasboeren appear to have rediscovered their attacking form as they prepare to visit a ground where they have already lost this year, suffering a 3-1 defeat to Zwolle in the third of last season’s three meetings.

AZ remain firmly in contention in what is shaping up to be an exciting title race, with only three points separating the top four in the Eredivisie table. The Cheese Farmers could end the weekend level on points with leaders PSV.

With two of their three league defeats so far coming on the road, where Sunday’s visitors are now five Eredivisie matches without a clean sheet, AZ certainly still have gears to find on their travels if they are to remain in the title conversation come the end of May.

PEC Zwolle finished just outside the bottom three last season, and their start to the 2026-27 campaign came as little surprise. They collected just four points from their opening eight matches, including a heavy 7-0 defeat to Feyenoord.

Taking over from interim Dennis van der Ree, Alex Pastoor made a winning start to life in the dugout thanks to a 3-1 win over Telstar, thanks to a Dylan Mbayo double and Ibrahim Cissoko’s early second-half strike.

The decision to part ways with Henry van der Vegt in October has since paid off, with Zwolle collecting 11 of a possible 15 points since his departure - the Eredivisie’s third-best return over that period.

Despite De Blauwvingers’ return to form, defeat this weekend could leave them just two points clear of the relegation zone ahead of their final three matches of 2026. Two of those fixtures are against current top-seven sides PSV and Fortuna Sittard.

Few teams are better placed to exploit AZ’s early-game struggles than Zwolle, who had opened the scoring in four of their previous five matches before their most recent victory, as well as in both of the last two meetings between the sides. Sunday's hosts will hope to strike early as they seek a third consecutive home league win.

Bulgarian international Filip Krastev has yet to feature for Zwolle this season as he continues to recover from an Achilles injury.

Eighteen-year-old Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus remain out of contention for the home side, who, however, have Sherel Floranus back available.

Attacking trio Jizz Hornkamp, Weslley Patati, and Mexx Meerdink are all unavailable for AZ, leaving them short of options up front.

Elijah Dijkstra, Stije Resink, Lewis Schouten, and Kees Smit will also miss Sunday’s match, with Resink yet to feature since March.

Ro-Zangelo Daal’s influential display off the bench in midweek took his tally to two goals and three assists in his last two appearances, making him one to watch.

Schendelaar; Burger, Graves, Viergever, Van der Haar; Thomas, Fichtinger; Mbayo, Namli, Cissoko; Van Hooijdonk

De Busser; Chavez, Hoedt, Goes, Maikuma; Stengs, Koopmeiners, Kwakman; Daal, Kovacs, Oufkir

AZ are dealing with several injury setbacks, which should give Zwolle some cause for optimism.

That said, the visitors remain favourites to win, and we expect them to edge a close contest.

#1680. Huge Manchester United injury blow as new Carlos Baleba injury return timeline confirmed

Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year after Mauricio Pochettino revealed the extent of his hamstring injury.

Baleba was injured during United’s Champions League clash against Roma on November 3, pulling up as he made a run into the penalty area before being forced off in tears.

The Cameroon international has not played since, with former manager Michael Carrick initially confirming he would be sidelined for several weeks.

Pochettino has now confirmed Baleba faces up to three months out, with the timeframe dating back to the injury against Roma. The setback is expected to rule him out throughout the festive period and potentially until the end of January.

“Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10 to 12 weeks,” Pochettino told a press conference on Friday.

Baleba is set to miss United’s upcoming fixtures against Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and RB Leipzig, as well as league matches against Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Brighton.

#1679. Miller ‘converting potential to being a performer’, says Revs boss Mitrovic

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

New England Revolution head coach Marko Mitrovic believes winger Peyton Miller is "converting from being potential to being a performer".

Miller made a decisive impact in the Revs' first-round, Game 1 victory over the Philadelphia Union in the MLS Cup playoff.

After forcing an own goal from Nathan Harriel, the 19-year-old scored in the second half to secure a 2-0 success at home.

Miller has scored eight goals and provided nine assists in MLS play this season, and Mitrovic praised the teenager's shift in mentality this term.

"He's converting from being potential to being a performer, and that's what a performer does," Mitrovic said of Miller.

"If I have to track 90 yards or 90 metres back and protect my goal, I have to do it. And if I have to attack, I have to do it.

"I think that level of maturity is actually the biggest progression that we've seen from Peyton this year."

— New England Revolution (@NERevolution) November 25, 2026

Ahead of their must-win game at Subaru Park, Philadelphia will be hoping to rely on a youngster of their own in Cavan Sullivan.

Sullivan was named 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year, and Union interim head coach Ryan Richter was delighted for the 17-year-old.

"All the good things that come to him are a reflection of the hard work and the mentality that he has," Richter said of Sullivan's award.

"The one thing that you know with him is that he has big ambitions and he has big dreams of what he wants to do in his career.

"This is a great honour for him, but I know he's not going to take it and get complacent. He's onto the next thing. He's driven to take another step after this."

Since the beginning of September, Damiani has scored 10 goals, tied for the most in MLS with Orlando City's Antoine Griezmann.

Meanwhile, his six goals in home matches in that span are tied for most in MLS with five players, including teammate Milan Iloski.

Miller (19 years, 13 days) became the first teenager to score a playoff goal for New England last weekend.

Prior to Miller, the youngest Revs goalscorer in the MLS Cup playoffs was Tajon Buchanan (21 years, 290 days) in 2020, also against the Union.

Philadelphia have lost just once at home against an MLS team since the start of April (W8 D5), but the loss came versus New England on October 24.

The Revs have won consecutive road matches against the Union once, winning both their away games in this fixture in 2015.

The Union have been shut out in three of their last four games, after not being held scoreless in any of their previous 20 matches against MLS foes.

The Game 1 win was New England's first shutout playoff victory since a 2–0 win over Philadelphia in the 2020 first round.

The Revs have posted consecutive shutout wins once in their playoff history, with 1–0 victories over the New York Red Bulls and Chicago Fire in 2007.

#1678. Liverpool XI vs Everton: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

Liverpool are full of confidence as they travel to face rivals Everton in the latest Merseyside derby on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola’s surging Reds have been piling up the goals since the November international break - scoring seven times across their last two fixtures alone.

A hugely satisfying 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United at Anfield last weekend in what was Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge of the visitors was quickly followed by a 3-0 victory in the Champions League away at Club Brugge.

Their two statement signings from last summer - Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - are both hitting top form, which bodes well for this weekend’s derby showdown.

Iraola will likely already know his starting XI for the short trip to Everton, based on the strong form of his team.

Stalwart Alisson will start in goal, while Virgil van Dijk will return to captain the side after being rested in Belgium on Wednesday night.

Ronald Araujo will be shifted to right-back as it is unlikely that Jeremie Frimpong will be asked to play twice in the span of five days following injury.

Jeremy Jacquet will partner Van Dijk in central defence, while Milos Kerkez looks set to make his 90th appearance under Iraola - the left-back having been trusted by his head coach at both Liverpool and Bournemouth.

Dominik Szoboszlai seems to have put his injury woes in the past, and while young Trey Nyoni has impressed when given opportunities this term, Alexis Mac Allister will surely get the nod alongside him in the midfield engine room as Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt with ongoing heel pain.

#1677. Calvin Bassey: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa sends "no chance" transfer message to Man United

By Ben Sully | 27 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:52

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out a January move for Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey.

Man United currently have the Premier League's second-worst defensive record after shipping 23 goals in 11 games.

As a result, the Red Devils are widely expected to bolster their backline when the transfer window opens for business in the new year.

Bassey is among those who have been mentioned as a potential target, having established himself as an accomplished Premier League centre-back during his time with Fulham.

However, Arbeloa has dampened Man United's hopes of a January swoop, insisting the focus is on agreeing a new contract with Bassey rather than entertaining the prospect of a winter sale.

“I’m so happy with Calvin and obviously he is not on sale," Arbeloa told reporters ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash against Bournemouth.

"No chance he can leave this club in January and I think he is happy here. He is one of our captains, he is one of our leaders.

"It is normal that so many clubs are interested in him, it is good for him and good for us. It means he is performing really well.

"We are working on a new contract, and I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bassey's current contract is set to expire at the end of the season, although Fulham hold the option to trigger a 12-month extension.

Speaking about last weekend's draw with Manchester City, Bassey said: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

"I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations."

Bassey has started all 11 of Fulham's Premier League games this season and has formed a strong central defensive partnership with summer signing David Affengruber.

The pair have helped Fulham build a five-game unbeaten league run in which they have conceded no more than one goal in any of the five matches.

#1676. Man City ‘close’ to major injury boost as Enzo Maresca reveals latest team news before Arsenal

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Antoine Semenyo is close to returning for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The Ghana international has not featured for Man City since sustaining a knee injury in the 3-2 victory over Ipswich on October 17, missing the last eight games across all competitions as a result.

During this period, City have not won a Premier League game and head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday to face leaders and reigning champions Arsenal.

Semenyo is not expected to be available for the trip to north London, though he could return against either Leeds or Brentford within the next week following a positive update from Maresca.

“We have good news, Antoine is quite close,” Maresca said in Friday’s pre-match press conference. “It’s good news for us. He is already on the pitch - he is very close, hopefully it can be next week, we hope so.

“I was laughing with him yesterday or two days ago. I told him in the Premier League the last game we won was with him on the pitch, so I said we need him back soon to win games.

“Antoine is an important player but we have more players in his position that are doing well like Iliman in this moment. But he needs time to recover.”

Semenyo had been enjoying a decent start to his first full season as a Man City player before being struck down by injury, scoring twice and weighing in with three assists in seven appearances.

The winger also started City’s big away wins over Manchester United and Liverpool, two results that has boosted Maresca’s belief that his side can end their recent slump with victory at Arsenal.

He added: “I think we already showed this season we are able to win important games, to win away. So I don’t see any reason why we are not able to win there.

“We have shown this season we can win important games away. Old Trafford and Anfield are two important away games and Sunday we have another one.

“We showed already and we can win again.”

#1674. Chelsea seal exciting midfielder signing after unexpected transfer twist

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally expected to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a pre-agreement contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their plans after he impressed during Chelsea trials.

Zongo made his senior international debut for Burkina Faso aged just 16 last month, when he came off the bench to play in the second half of a 7-0 friendly defeat by Argentina in Buenos Aires.

The teenager previously impressed when he starred for Burkina Faso on their run to the quarter-finals of the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar last autumn. The midfielder scored the winner as his nation stunned Germany in the round of 16.

Scouts from a number of top European clubs were in attendance at games across the tournament and many took note of the performances produced by Zongo, who was 15 at the time.

Zongo had previously been linked with several other suitors, including LaLiga outfit Villarreal.

#1673. Why Man United could be missing skipper Bruno Fernandes for Premier League showdown with Brentford

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 13:50, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:56

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has revealed that captain Bruno Fernandes is a major doubt for Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford due to an illness.

Fernandes was unable to train on Friday, having picked up a virus.

Pochettino has said that no final decision has been made on the Portugal international at this stage of proceedings, but he is a major doubt for the game with the Bees.

"We will not take any risks. We will see when he wakes up tomorrow," Pochettino told reporters during Friday's press conference at Carrington.

There has been criticism of Fernandes' form this season, but he has still come up with eight goals and three assists in 16 appearances for the Red Devils during the 2026-27 campaign.

The 32-year-old scored twice against his former club Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night and had been in line to start against Brentford.

Fernandes now has four goals and one assist in five Champions League appearances this season, in addition to four goals and two assists in 10 Premier League matches.

Man United will also again be missing Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford through injury this weekend, but Luke Shaw returned to the bench against Sporting and could potentially receive some minutes in this contest.

The Red Devils will be going in search of just their second Premier League win of the campaign against Brentford.

A disastrous campaign to date has left the Red Devils in 19th spot in the Premier League table, claiming only eight points from their first 11 games of the season.

"This is a group of players who want to do well, who want to perform. Our job is to build confidence. We arrive full of energy, positive, but it's difficult for the players when the results haven't been up to scratch, but we try to help them as best we can," added Pochettino.

Man United have lost two of their last three Premier League matches against Brentford, but they recorded a 2-1 win over the Bees in the corresponding game earlier this season.

#1672. Bastoni could miss remainder of 2026 as Inter gear up for Genoa double header

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Inter centre-back Alessandro Bastoni has suffered a left quadriceps strain, with reports indicating he will miss Saturday's meeting with Genoa and may not return until 2027.

The Nerazzurri confirmed on Friday that Bastoni had undergone tests in the wake of Wednesday's 2-0 Champions League victory over Stuttgart, in which Bastoni only lasted 41 minutes before being replaced by Federico Dimarco.

Bastoni has made 15 appearances for Inter across all competitions, with all 15 of those being starts. The only outfielder to better his 1,199 minutes for Cristian Chivu's side in 2026-27 is midfielder Nicolo Barella (1,298).

Bastoni has won 45 of the 79 duels he has contested this term, including 14 of 20 in the air, helping Inter win 29 points from the first 12 games of their Scudetto defence.

A club statement said: "Alessandro Bastoni underwent clinical and diagnostic tests this morning at the Humanitas Institute in Rozzano.

"The tests revealed a strain to his left quadriceps."

Inter did not offer a timeline for Bastoni's recovery, but with widespread reports indicating he could miss at least three weeks, he may not return until the new year.

Inter have seven games to play before New Year's Eve, the last of which is a Supercoppa Italiana final showdown with Lazio on December 22, a little over three weeks away.

Despite Inter's strong points haul, they sit third in Serie A ahead of Genoa's visit to San Siro, behind Lazio and Roma.

Yet Chivu was impressed by his players' reaction against Stuttgart in midweek, after their previous game saw them squander a 4-2 lead in a 4-4 draw with Atalanta.

"We didn't lose clarity of mind after the game in Bergamo: we played well for 75 minutes, but the final stages don't define the good things we produced in that match," he said.

"To tell the truth, you have to remain clear-headed and analyse what happened from a technical and mental point of view."

Inter will face Genoa twice in the space of three days, with the teams also being drawn together in the Coppa Italia's round of 16. The Grifone are 10th in Serie A, having beaten Sassuolo 2-0 away from home last time out.

Esposito, at the age of 21 years and 147 days, became the fourth-youngest player to score 12+ Serie A goals for Inter in the three-points-for-a-win era last week, behind Mario Balotelli (19 years and 78 days), Obafemi Martins (20 years and 17 days) and Ronaldo Nazario (21 years and 146 days).

If he scores a brace here (21 years and 153 days old on Saturday), he would become the third-youngest to reach 15 goals for the Nerazzurri, surpassing Ronaldo, who achieved this milestone at 21 years and 159 days.

Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances since arriving from Preston North End.

Among players in their debut Serie A seasons, in the three-points-for-a-win era, only Diego Milito (11 in 2008-09) and Krzysztof Piatek (10 in 2018-19) have netted more goals in the first 13 games of a campaign for Genoa.

Inter are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A matches against Genoa (W11 D3). Among current top-flight teams, they only have a longer ongoing unbeaten run against Atalanta (16).

At home, meanwhile, the Nerazzurri have posted 12 straight league wins over Genoa, keeping a clean sheet in 10 of those games and only conceding two goals in total.

Throughout their top-flight history, Inter have only registered a longer run of successive home wins against Como (15).

Inter's firepower should prove too much for Genoa here, too, as they have scored in each of their last 22 Serie A matches, netting 57 times in total at an average of 2.6 per game.

They have also won six in a row at home in Serie A, scoring at least two goals in each of those matches.

The Nerazzurri last enjoyed a longer Serie A winning streak at San Siro between October 2023 and March 2024 (nine in a row), while they last had a longer run while scoring multiple goals in every game between October 2016 and February 2017 (eight in a row).
