#1652. Will Man City be stripped of Premier League titles? Possible sanctions amid new update before Arsenal showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

Man Utd defender at risk of suspension after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Liverpool handed new suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Fines: City could also face substantial financial penalties. The club could be ordered to pay fines, compensation or costs associated with the proceedings.

The sanctions process is separate from the commission’s determination on the charges, meaning City’s punishment remains to be decided.

Man United welcome the Bees to Old Trafford on Saturday seeking a first league victory since August in what will be Mauricio Pochettino’s home debut as head coach.

#1650. Crystal Palace vs. Hull City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 14:54

Fresh from their first victory under Thomas Frank on Thursday, Crystal Palace welcome Hull City to Selhurst Park in Sunday's matchweek 13 encounter aiming to end their five-match losing league run.

The bottom-placed Eagles sit nine places below their visitors in the Premier League table but hope to draw inspiration from their Europa League success and collect maximum points in the Dane's first home top-flight fixture.

After conceding a late winner against Coventry City on Frank's managerial debut for Palace last weekend, the capital club enjoyed a change of fortune as Dwight McNeil struck in the 81st minute to secure their second European victory.

The winger's goal sealed Palace's first win since beating Fulham in the EFL Cup a month ago, and they now seek consecutive victories for the first time since overcoming the Cottagers and Middlesbrough in the league and domestic cup respectively in early September.

That ambition will be difficult to realise for the Eagles, whose inability to keep clean sheets continues to undermine them, with Mamadou Sarr's 66th-minute goal marking a fifth consecutive match in which the Londoners have conceded.

Their EFL Cup shutout remains Palace's only clean sheet in 11 matches, underlining their broader problems, particularly when they cannot rely on Jean-Philippe Mateta's usual attacking influence.

It remains to be seen whether Frank can address those weaknesses before Sunday's encounter, as the bottom-placed Eagles pursue their first league victory since early October's 3-1 success over Nottingham Forest in an attempt to escape the relegation zone.

Hull's modest scoring figures may not frighten the division's worst defence, but Sergej Jakirovic will know that Coventry were hardly prolific before scoring three in last weekend's 3-2 victory over Palace to reach 13 league goals.

The Tigers also have 13 goals after 11 matches, exceeding Coventry's tally before last weekend and suggesting that the promoted outfit can threaten the division's leakiest defence.

Last season's Championship playoff winners travel to Selhurst Park buoyed by their victory over Brighton & Hove Albion, secured through two goals in second-half stoppage time to end a three-month wait for maximum points in the competition.

That success lifted Jakirovic's team to 11th in the Premier League table, and consecutive victories for the first time since the opening two gameweeks could propel them into the top half, with their 14 points just three short of sixth-placed Brentford.

Having remained difficult to beat throughout their three-month winless spell, Hull now hope to leave any anxiety behind and find the consistency to demonstrate that they belong at this level.

Mateta will serve the final game of his suspension this weekend, while Yeremy Pino is also banned after collecting his fifth yellow card of the season in the defeat to Coventry.

With Ismaila Sarr also unavailable due to a groin problem, the Eagles are missing several potential match-winners and will look to McNeil and Jorgen Strand Larsen, who has already registered one goal and two assists under Frank.

Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) are also sidelined for the hosts on Sunday.

Hull also have several injury concerns: Charlie Hughes will be assessed before the trip to south London, while Hidemasa Morita (muscle), Ilyas Ansah (back), Joe Gelhardt (thigh), Matt Targett (ankle), Eliot Matazo (knee) and Tim Iroegbunam (thigh) are also carrying injuries.

Oli McBurnie and Mohamed Belloumi were instrumental in the Tigers' latest victory, with McBurnie scoring both late goals and Belloumi providing one assist to take their respective goal contributions for the season to six apiece.

Henderson; Khalaili, Richards, Disasi, Mitchell; Timber, Wharton; McNeil, Kamada, Guessand; Strand Larsen

Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Gourna-Douath; Belloumi, Crooks, Thomas; McBurnie

Palace may struggle to build on Thursday's victory without Mateta, Pino and Sarr, particularly with the quick turnaround limiting Frank's preparation time.

Hull remained competitive throughout their prolonged winless spell, and McBurnie's decisive display against Brighton suggests that the visitors could punish another defensive lapse to edge this encounter.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta will have his attacking options bolstered for the visit of Manchester City in the Premier League this weekend.

The reigning Premier League champions welcome an out-of-form Man City side to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday afternoon and will be looking to avoid their winless run stretching to three games.

While Arsenal have lead in both games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund in the past week, they have failed to win any of their games since returning from the international break.

Missing from the matchday squad at St James' Park last weekend was Max Dowman as he served the final game of a three-match suspension after being sent-off in the shock Carabao Cup fourth round loss to Fleetwood Town.

The Gunners unsuccessfully appealed for the red card to be overturned, meaning the teenager had to sit out wins over Liverpool and Hull, as well as the 2-2 draw against Newcastle.

Dowman was on the bench against Dortmund but did not come on, though he has now been cleared to feature in domestic matches for Arsenal and is an option as Arteta aims to get his attack firing again.

“When the margin is by one goal, especially with the level of the opponent that we play every three days, how difficult it is; they just need a moment, and it happened with Dortmund,” Arteta said in the pre-match press conference.

“They broke the press after eliminating one of our front players, and they have the capacity to pick out that player, that player has an individual action, and then it’s a goal.

“They didn’t do much more than that, but that was enough to get a point and you have to assume that. But again, overall, if we continue to generate what we’re generating, I’m very positive that things are going to be good.”

In addition to Dowman, David Raya is on course to be available against Man City as Arteta revealed the goalkeeper is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder issue.

#1647. Chelsea: Why Wesley Fofana avoided a red card against Nottingham Forest as Xabi Alonso forced into change

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana found himself at the centre of controversy during the Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest.

With the Blues trailing to an Igor Jesus goal, Fofana gave his team-mates an even bigger mountain to climb early in the second half at the City Ground on Friday night.

After misjudged the bounce of the ball, thus allowing ex-Chelsea striker Liam Delap to latch onto the long ball and advance towards goal, the Frenchman panicked in an attempt to recover and ended up making a rash challenge in the box and conceded a penalty in the process.

Morgan Gibbs-White made no mistake from the spot to double Forest's lead, though Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit three minutes later to give Xabi Alonso's side hope of avoiding a third straight defeat.

Fofana’s additional punishment for the tackle was a yellow card, though there has been some questions asked on social media as to why he was not sent-off.

Ultimately, the Premier League have provided an explanation as to why.

A statement reads: “The referee’s call of penalty to Nottingham Forest and yellow card for Fofana for the challenge on Delap was checked and confirmed by VAR.

“VAR: “It's clearly inside, the main contact is with the leg and upper body. So it’s inside, the penalty’s fine and the yellow card's fine”.”

Alonso reacted immediately to the threat of Fofana being sent-off for two bookable offences by substituting the central defender, replacing him with Levi Colwill who had been dropped in favour of Moises Caicedo starting in central defence.

That introduction did not have the impact the Chelsea boss would have hoped for as Gibbs-White ran off the back of Caicedo to restore Forest’s two-goal lead and leave the visitors staring another defeat in the face.

#1646. Leeds United, Fulham suffer 'extraordinary' blow in pursuit for 11-goal striker target ahead of January window

By Carter White | 27 Nov 2026 14:53, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 15:01

Leeds United and Fulham have reportedly suffered a major blow to their respective pursuits of signing Racing de Santander striker Yassir Zabiri.

Daniel Farke's side have been in the business of getting their own house in order recently, announcing a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Ao Tanaka until the end of the 2028-29 campaign.

Leading Leeds' goalscoring ranks in the Premier League this term, Dominic Calvert-Lewin lead the way for the 28-year-old maestro, with the England international  also signing new terms.

As for matters in West London, Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham went down the La Liga route during the summer transfer window, looking to replace high-profile departures Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson.

It was claimed earlier in the season that members of the Craven Cottage playing staff were unhappy with the situation at the club following the arrival of the former Real Madrid manager.

According to Spanish publication SER Cantabria via El Desmarque, Premier League clubs Leeds and Fulham have suffered a major blow in their potential pursuits of Zaibiri ahead of the January transfer window.

The 21-year-old is currently on loan at Racing Santander from French club Rennes, who supposedly have no option to recall the youngster from his spell in Spain until the end of the season.

The report states that Les Rennais would need to pay Racing Santander an 'extraordinary' amount of compensation to recall Zabiri during the January trading point - a move that would allow a permanent sale of the star.

Leeds, Fulham and Ipswich Town are the known Premier League suitors for the attacker, who recently made his Morocco senior debut during the November international break, scoring against Niger.

However, those English clubs could be blown out of the water by the other horses in this particular transfer race, with Spanish powerhouses Barcelona and Real Madrid said to be interested in the talent.

Netting on 11 occasions across his opening 13 top-flight appearances of the season, Zabiri is only bested by Raphinha (15) and Kylian Mbappe (13) in La Liga's Golden Boot race after 13 games.

The 21-year-old burst onto the Racing Santander stage with a hat-trick against Elche in August before continuing his attacking antics into the autumn, recently bagging a brace in the victory over Real Sociedad.

The world-class form of Zabiri has caught the eye of some of Europe's biggest clubs, so it appears that the likes of Leeds and Fulham are set to be muscled out of a move for the Moroccan sensation.

#1644. Bassett urges Portland to ‘set the tone’ in must-win clash with Dallas

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Portland Timbers midfielder Cole Bassett believes they must set the tone against FC Dallas in Game 2 of their MLS Cup Playoff clash.

Dallas cruised to a 3-0 victory in Game 1, with Joaquin Valiente scoring a brace before Sam Sarver added a third goal in second-half stoppage time.

That defeat saw Portland's four-game winning run in MLS play come to an end, but they can keep the series alive with a victory at Providence Park on Saturday.

Bassett has urged his team-mates to make a fast start in front of their home fans, insisting an early goal could make the difference.

"We're in professional sports here. This is a big game, a must-win," Bassett told reporters.

"And you have to play, because all it takes is one moment, at the end of the day, to turn it around.

"We love playing in front of them [the fans], and we know Providence Park is going to be rocking this weekend.

"But there are little things that I think can help: the first duel, first tackle, kind of setting the tone for the match.

"One of the keys against this Dallas team is scoring. For us, an early goal or a first-half goal is huge."

Portland head coach Marti Cifuentes added: "I do know that in the playoffs, [with] every kind of adversity, you need to be mentally strong to approach that.

"And I think this group has been showing that. So, of course, we're going to learn from what happened in Dallas.

"We need to make sure that all that anger that you feel after losing a game, that you need to be ready to push.

"What better occasion than to do it at home in front of our fans, who always help us?"

An opportunity to get even comes knocking  Let’s get this building rocking  https://t.co/QkBY3Dlww2

— Portland Timbers (@TimbersFC) November 26, 2026

Velde has two goals in five career playoff games with Portland, including an effort in the team's last home playoff match in 2025.

Only four Timbers players have more postseason goals in the club's MLS history: Diego Valeri (six), Sebastian Blanco (five), Dairon Asprilla (four) and Felipe Mora (four).

In the first match of this series with Portland, Valiente became the fourth Dallas player to score a brace in a playoff game.

Valiente joined Carlos Ruiz (2005), Ariel Graziani (1999) and Dante Washington (1997) as the Dallas players to score multiple goals in a playoff match.

While Dallas stormed to victory in Game 1, the Opta supercomputer has predicted a closer matchup on Saturday, in a match which would be decided by penalties if it ends even after 90 minutes.

Dallas' 3–0 win in Game 1 was tied for their largest margin of victory in a playoff match. The club also secured 3–0 victories against the LA Galaxy in the 2010 conference finals and the 1997 conference semi-finals.

Dallas are now unbeaten in their last seven matches (W4 D3) against Portland and earned their first postseason victory in five tries (D2 L2). Dallas have won just once in 18 road games against the Timbers (D8 L9), with that victory coming in April 2016.

Portland have been shut out in back-to-back playoff games for the first time in club history. The Timbers allowed at least three goals in both of those defeats, joining Inter Miami (2020–22) as the only teams in MLS Cup playoff history with consecutive shutout defeats by three or more goals.

Milan have lost three of their opening four games in the competition and they are running out of runway to put things right. With 12 points up for grabs, the feeling is that the Rossoneri need at least a couple of wins to even get a play-off spot, given they sit outside the top 24 at present.

#1642. Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Pressure increases on Xabi Alonso after third successive defeat

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea slumped to a third successive Premier League defeat as they went down 3-2 at Nottingham Forest to mount the pressure on boss Xabi Alonso.

Chelsea player ratings: Defender handed 3/10 for ‘critical error’

Why Chelsea star was not shown a red card against Nottingham Forest

Arsenal selection boost confirmed ahead of Man City showdown

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

The Blues were second-best to Forest, who won it through Igor Jesus’ brilliant opener and a Morgan Gibbs-White double after the break.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that does not mask the overall poor performance.

The latest loss comes after last weekend’s alarming 4-1 defeat to Leeds and Alonso has clear issues to address as they slide down the table.

One of them is Wesley Fofana after the Frenchman was booed and jeered by his own fans after an unauthorised YouTube interview where he appeared to joke about the club’s Carabao Cup exit.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

Alonso opted to change his defence after last week’s debacle against Leeds, dropping Levi Colwill and replacing him in the back four with midfielder Moises Caicedo.

The Spaniard did stick with under-fire Fofana, who was booed from the off. Both men came under early pressure as Forest began well.

Liam Delap, desperate to score against the club where his career stalled last season, had a snap-shot in the first minute, but Emiliano Martinez was not troubled.

But the Argentina goalkeeper could do nothing about a sublime Forest opener in the fifth minute. Daniel Munoz drilled in a cross from that right that Jesus sent into the top corner with an acrobatic volley. It was a fine piece of athleticism, even if contact did come off the shin.

That was the only real moment of quality in a first half where Forest were the better side. Alonso’s men had nothing going forward and failed to muster a shot on target.

Things did not improve after the break as Fofana’s night got worse. He lost out on a routine challenge to Delap, who burst clear into the box and was felled by the Frenchman.

Referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot and Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way.

But Chelsea got themselves back into it three minutes later, with their first shot on target, and they needed plenty of luck.

Pedro Neto’s shot hit Jair Cunha and it fell kindly into the path of half-time substitute Emegha, who rifled into the bottom corner.

Fofana was then hooked as he was put out of his mercy, but Chelsea still looked vulnerable.

James McAtee should have done better with his shot after a fine pass by Gibbs-White, while Murillo’s thumping volley from distance brought a good save by Martinez.

Forest restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute as they scored an excellent third.

Xaver Schlager picked up a loose ball, made space with a fine first touch and then found Gibbs-White with an incisive pass, which the England international coolly clipped home.

They appeared to be seeing the match out with ease, but that changed in the 89th minute as Chelsea scored out of nothing.

Neto’s cross found Emegha who headed home to set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

#1641. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

#MUNMCI – 23'The referee's call of red card to Foden for violent conduct was checked and confirmed by VAR.REF: "Red card Phil Foden – kick out into the body of Bruno".VAR: "That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement. Confirming the red card for…

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

If you haven’t checked out the interview, you can have a read here

Fans have chanted: “You treat us like s--- Ratcliffe and the Glazers, you treat us like s---.”

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a new 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

"An absolute WORLDIE from range!"Lewis Dunk scores a contender for goal of the season 🤯 pic.twitter.com/m5bPzm5Wm3

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

There are hundreds upon hundreds of #MUFC supporters pouring through the Munich tunnel protesting against the Glazers and Ratcliffe's ownership and running of the club pic.twitter.com/VlhkMoxbmI

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

Manchester City XI: Donnarumma, Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Reis, Bouaddi, O’Reilly, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis

Your Manchester derby line-up! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Nunes, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovačić, Reis, Bouaddi, O'Reilly, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/9h5CGprFaF

It is a very offensive-minded XI with Dorgu at full-back and a midfield trio of Tielemans, Fernandes and Mainoo behind Mbeumo, Cunha and Rashford. The results could be spectacular, but City should fancy punching holes in that set up.

Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mbeumo, Cunha, Fernandes, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Heaven, Mazraoui, Yoro, Mount, Santos, Lacey, Sesko, Zirkzee.

Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1640. Man United transfer news: Truth behind English club's pursuit of Argentina superstar Nico Paz 'revealed'

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 14:59, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United are reportedly interested in Como attacker Nico Paz ahead of next summer's transfer window.

The 22-year-old has been in impressive form for Como during the 2026-27 campaign, coming up with six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances in all competitions.

Paz has three goals and three assists in 11 Serie A appearances this season, while he has excelled in the Champions League for Cesc Fabregas' team, coming up with three goals and five assists in five appearances in the league stage of the tournament.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Paz's future with Como.

Paz arrived at Como from Real Madrid in the summer of 2024, and he has represented the Italian team on 91 occasions, scoring 25 goals and registering 25 assists.

Paz has a contract with Como until the summer of 2028, but Real Madrid do have the option to re-sign Paz for £67m next year.

Man United have allegedly activated a further year on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract to take him to the summer of 2028, but there is still uncertainty surrounding the Portugal international's future.

According to The Athletic, the 20-time English champions view Paz as a potential replacement for Fernandes, should the experienced attacker leave Old Trafford.

Journalist David Ornstein claims that Paz is not currently looking to return to Real Madrid, allegedly as he is unsure how much football he would receive due to the presence of Jude Bellingham in the number 10 position at Bernabeu.

Man United are said to appeal to Paz, even considering their current struggles, with the Red Devils expected to be in the race for the Argentina international in 2027.

Paz shares an agent with new Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, which has also allegedly strengthened the English club's hand when it comes to a potential race.

The attacker is a 16-time Argentina international, scoring six goals and registering two assists for his country, and is currently viewed as one of the best playmakers in world football.

#1639. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta reveals conditions for January transfer as Gunners track Antonio Nusa

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has insisted Arsenal are open to a transfer "opportunity" if it presents itself in the January window.

The Gunners sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League but questions remain over the forward options in the squad.

Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were all sold in the summer, with only Christos Tzolis signed to bolster the attack.

Arsenal have scored 17 goals in the league this season, the worst record of the club's currently in the top six, and have been punished for wasteful displays in the last week against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund.

RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa is among the players Arsenal are tracking, but January has historically been a quiet window for the Gunners.

Not since 2023, when Arsenal brought in Jorginho, Leandro Trossard and Jakub Kiwior mid-season, have the club made a January signing.

However, Arteta insisted Arsenal were working hard in all of those windows, even when no business was done, and he is confident the club will be alert to potential deals again this time.

“We've always been very active in the transfer window, especially when we have certain issues," Arteta said.

"Have we managed to get a deal over the line? Sometimes not. So we will see if there is an opportunity there and something that we believe is going to make a difference for the team."

Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke is expected in London next week and he is set to meet with Arteta and the club's hierarchy.

The January window will be one of the items on the agenda, though Arteta was keen to emphasise that the club have already been putting transfer plans in place.

“We don’t wait to talk about these things only when it is face to face," Arteta said of Kroenke's trip to London.

#1638. ‘We don’t take anyone apart’ – Alonso stands by Chelsea defender Fofana

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Xabi Alonso insisted Chelsea "don't take anyone apart" after Wesley Fofana came under more criticism in their defeat to Nottingham Forest.

Chelsea lost 3-2 at the City Ground on Friday after Igor Jesus' volley and a brace from Morgan Gibbs-White secured victory for Forest, despite Emmanuel Emegha's double for the Blues.

Since the start of March, Chelsea have lost 14 of their 23 Premier League games (W7 D2) – the most of any side in the competition in this period.

Chelsea have conceded 23 goals in the Premier League this season – only bottom side Crystal Palace (27) have shipped more.

In fact, it is the Blues' joint-most in their opening 12 matches of a campaign in the competition (also 23 in 2015-16).

Fofana, who was booed by his own fans after a recent interview in which he appeared to joke about missing the decisive penalty in an EFL Cup defeat to Liverpool, gave away a penalty for Forest's second goal after a clumsy challenge on Liam Delap.

The Frenchman was then replaced by Levi Colwill, who was benched for makeshift centre-back Moises Caicedo, but Alonso has called for togetherness during a difficult spell.

"We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support," Alonso told Sky Sports when asked about Fofana.

Defeat in Nottingham. #CFC | #NFOCHE https://t.co/M4LPYhOVll

— Chelsea FC (@ChelseaFC) November 27, 2026

"We know we have to go through difficult moments and we don't take apart anyone and we want to help and stick together.

"It's a difficult moment for everyone. It's disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can't stop.

"We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions."

Alonso has now lost as many of his 15 games as Chelsea manager in all competitions as he did in 34 games in charge of previous club Real Madrid (six).

#1637. How Xabi Alonso decisions backfired to plunge Chelsea further into crisis

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea are embroiled in a crisis. They look like one of the worst teams in the Premier League right now.

That is the reality their highly-regarded manager Xabi Alonso and expensively-assembled squad must accept they find themselves in after Friday night’s grim 3-2 loss to Nottingham Forest, their fourth league defeat in five games.

Alonso and his players must share the responsibility for another incoherent performance from a team that looks so recently cobbled together that watching them makes you feel as though it is August, not three months into the season.

The manager got some selection decisions wrong. Dropping Levi Colwill instead of Wesley Fofana at centre-back was an eyebrow-raiser before kick-off and was punished brutally when Fofana — not exactly having a cracker of a week — was turned inside out by his former team-mate Liam Delap and then fouled him to concede a penalty from Chelsea’s one-goal deficit became two.

Cue a yellow card, Fofana subbed off for Colwill, and Alonso left facing questions.

Similarly alongside Fofana, where Moises Caicedo was shifted back from midfield to centre-back but was error-prone all night and had an off day, much like Chelsea, who are getting used to having those.

Further forward, Danny Welbeck was ineffectual and, if anything, seemed to repel the ball. At half-time he was replaced by Emmanuel Emegha, who scored Chelsea’s only goal at Leeds last Saturday, now went on to net both of their goals at Forest, and will have been left wondering why he had not been picked to start the game even more so than when the teamsheet was first read out to the squad.

Xabi Alonso reacts to Wesley Fofana boos with message to Chelsea fans

Xabi Alonso makes Emmanuel Emegha prediction after Chelsea impact

Arteta reveals conditions for January transfer as Arsenal track Nusa

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

His two goals were striker’s finishes from speculative crosses, goals that just sort of seemed to happen rather than being the product of a flowing move here or a well-formed pattern of play there. Chelsea did none of that, again. Against Sunderland, Leeds and now Forest, they have been confused, confusing and toothless.

In this rotten period where they have so missed the injured striker Joao Pedro and centre-back Maxence Lacroix, they have shown an incredible ability to play people into form. They played Sunderland into form before the international break and now came a gift-wrapped brace for goal-shy Morgan Gibbs-White.

Where Chelsea go from here is really anyone’s guess. Hosting the division’s bottom side Crystal Palace on Wednesday is, on the face of it, a kind fixture. But the last time they faced 20th in the table, they lost at Sunderland and failed to even score.

Most concerning of all for Alonso and his coaching staff will have been how effective Forest’s high-intensity approach to the game proved. A committed press against a confidence-shot defence earned them a victory over Chelsea that future opponents will watch back and surely believe to be repeatable.

That is all their free weeks on the training ground with no European football for disruption has gained them.

This crisis of confidence appears to be teaching their opponents more about Chelsea than it is teaching Chelsea about themselves.

#1632. ‘Three or four’: Roberto De Zerbi outlines Tottenham transfer plans

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham are “three or four positions” away from completing the squad rebuild.

After securing Premier League survival on the final day of last season, Spurs moved aggressively and decisively in the summer transfer window, twice breaking their transfer record to sign midfielders Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali for a combined £185m.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke signed from Brighton for around £52m, while Savio arrived later in the window from Manchester City for a fee that could reach £85m if all add-ons are met.

Omar Marmoush also swapped City for Spurs, signing on loan with a conditional £60m obligation to buy at the end of the season, while Spurs further bolstered their squad with the free transfers of Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson.

A mammoth summer of spending then came to a close on deadline day when Chelsea pair Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk arrived at Hotspur Way.

Spurs have undergone seismic changes over the last six months and finally appear to be bearing the fruits of their labour and sizeable financial outlay, with De Zerbi’s side winning four of their last five games.

Tottenham XI vs Sunderland: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Transfer news LIVE: Paz to Arsenal twist; Man Utd boost; Chelsea shock

Chelsea seal exciting midfielder signing after unexpected transfer twist

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

The club’s position on and off the pitch is a far cry from the dire situation they found themselves in when De Zerbi took charge of his first game away to Sunderland in May, with the club mired in relegation trouble.

A 1-0 defeat that afternoon had Spurs seriously thinking about the possibility of life in the Championship. But as De Zerbi prepares to return to the Stadium of Light for the first time since that near-fateful day, he admits Spurs need just three or four more additions to complete their squad.

“As a team, as a squad, I think we are in a very good position because we, I think we made a great session of the transfer market. We changed ten, twelve players, and we brought all first targets in the window,” De Zerbi said.

“And for the future, I think we don't need in too many positions. I think we need to finish the squad. Yes, in maybe three, four positions, and then we have not to move too many players.

“We need to stay together. We need to improve the connection, the relationships. Improve the style of play, the quality of the play. To improve the mentality, but I think we are in the good way to become better and to do something special for this club.”

Having finished just one point above the relegation zone last season, Spurs have not had to contend with European football this term, allowing De Zerbi precious time on the training pitch to instil his ideas.

They are now, though, approaching a run of nine games in five weeks that will test their squad’s durability and increased depth as injuries continue to hamper them.

Despite their injury issues, De Zerbi believes his squad have an advantage heading into the festive period, with Spurs enjoying more time to rest, recover and prepare for matches in the first few months of the season.

“Yes, I think it is a big advantage,” De Zerbi continued before acknowledging that the benefit of one game per week only works in the first full season when you are trying to build principles and identity.

“For sure, the first season when you are working on the basis of the team, it’s better playing one game per week.

“But if you are from two, three, four seasons already on the bench, I think nothing changed because you have a stronger squad, you have a stronger principle of the play.

“You have not to lose too much time preparing the game or giving information, giving principles. The players in two seasons, they already know everything.

“Yes, you can prepare in the more details the game, more strategy and less principle. While now we are working more in principle and less in the strategy, but at the end it's part of the journey. It's a natural journey.”

#1631. Gibbs-White ‘trusting the process’ under Glasner at Forest

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Morgan Gibbs-White has called for calm around Nottingham Forest as they are "trusting the process" under Oliver Glasner.

The Tricky Trees secured another crucial home Premier League win this season on Friday after defeating Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground.

Igor Jesus gave Forest an early lead before Gibbs-White and Emmanuel Emegha scored braces at either end in the second half.

Gibbs-White has scored 15 Premier League goals in 2026; only Erling Haaland (17) has scored more.

Against Chelsea, he scored more than once in a match in the competition for just the second time in his 202 appearances, after his hat-trick against Burnley in April last season.

Forest have won back-to-back home games in the Premier League for the first time since April 2025.

Before their wins over Manchester City and now Chelsea, the Tricky Trees had won just one of their previous 15 league matches at the City Ground (D8 L6).

Gibbs-White believes Glasner deserves time to prove himself in the Forest dugout after a slow start to the season.

"I think there's going to be drama no matter what – it's the Premier League, there's always going to be drama," the Forest captain told Sky Sports.

"But I feel we need to take a bit of realisation that we have a new manager, we're sticking with him, we're trusting the process, believing in him and trusting what he wants.

"Not every week is it going to be pretty or is it going to be nice, but when times like this happen, we've got to make the most of it and enjoy it.

#1630. Arsenal vs. Man City: Enzo Maresca is “not a magician” as Citizens boss addresses slump, Premier League title talk

By Oliver Thomas | 27 Nov 2026 15:10, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 15:13

Enzo Maresca views Manchester City’s upcoming away clash against Premier League champions Arsenal as a true measure of his side's current standing.

The Citizens travel to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday sitting third in the Premier League table and six points behind leaders Arsenal, who have won nine of their first 11 games this season (D1 L1).

After winning 11 of their first 12 games in all competitions this term, Man City have now won just two of their last seven matches, with one of those victories - at home to Brighton in the EFL Cup - coming after a penalty shootout.

Man City are without a win in four Premier League games, with three straight defeats followed by a frustrating 1-1 draw with Fulham last weekend, while they were also held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Defensive frailties have been a major factor behind City’s recent slump, with Maresca’s side failing to keep a clean sheet in any of their last 10 matches and conceding 20 goals in that time.

Discussing why City’s form has dropped off at a press conference on Friday, Maresca told reporters: "It's more than easy to understand why because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.

“Probably because we won seven games in a row, eight with the Champions League, everyone was thinking that there was no transition.

"I said many times, I'm not a magician. There's a transition, it's normal. We have eight or nine new players, the manager is new, so you need time.

"You can see with different clubs when they transition, how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal. I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all, understanding that we need to win games because it's our business. For me, it's all normal."

Despite the shadow of Man City’s high-profile guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, Maresca’s squad entered the campaign as one of the primary threats to Arsenal's crown.

However, the Sky Blues now risk falling nine points adrift of the league leaders – a deficit that many believe would effectively extinguish their title ambitions for the season.

"To be honest, for sure I'm worried about game-by-game but I'm focused about our team,” Maresca said when asked whether his team can afford to fall further behind Arsenal.

"How we can improve, how we be better, how we can be more solid, how we can attack more. I know in the present it's important but the future is important to understand and improve and build something with the team."

Asked whether results are causing confidence issues with players, the Italian added: "For sure, when you don't win games, it's not the ideal situation, but we won games at the beginning.

"We have also seven or eight new players that need to be used to winning games, so it's just a process."

Despite this, Maresca remains optimistic ahead of Sunday’s contest and believes that it is "useless" to think about where Man City would finish in the table at the end of the season at this stage of the campaign.

He said: "Where we can be on Sunday night if we win, lose or draw, it's important but it's a long season. We'll see where we are in February and March and from there you can set the goals.

"Now, I think it's useless speaking about targets or where we can be at the end of the season.

"[Arsenal] won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final (last season). That shows how good they are in this moment.

"Not just with the central defender (Gabriel Magalhaes) but with [Declan] Rice or Bruno [Guimaraes] if he's playing, you need to win duels and second balls.

“You need to show personality. That's why it's also a nice game for us to see where we are in terms of personality and from there try to understand the situation.”

"We're going to try our best to win the game but, no doubt, they are probably the best,” Maresca continued: “The problem for us has been quite clear between what we create and what we concede."

“I think we have already shown this season that we are able to win important games, to win away. I don't see any reason why we are not able to win there."

Meanwhile, Maresca has provided a positive update on the fitness of key attacker Antoine Semenyo and has revealed when he could return to first-team action.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso has pleaded with fans to support Wesley Fofana after the Chelsea defender had a night to forget against Nottingham Forest.

The Blues defender, who has been singled out for poor performances during the Chelsea’s bad run of form, needed a strong show, having spoken for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics.

Fofana admitted that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month’s Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

He apologised for the interview and Alonso said the matter was closed.

“We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. He has apologised," Alonso told reporters in the pre-match press conference.

“It was not right, he has said it is not going to be repeated, these types of things.”

However, Friday’s Premier League game at the City Ground was a bad one for the Frenchman.

The visiting supporters jeered the Fofana when he was in possession in the first half and a bad night got worse in the early stages of the second half when he brought down Liam Delap for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted to double Forest’s lead.

He was substituted soon after, following chants from travelling Blues fans of “f*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.”

Speaking after the 3-2 loss to Forest, Alonso jumped to the defence of Fofana, insisting now is the time for solidarity as Chelsea aim to arrest a poor run of form.

#1628. Amorim explains selection choices, Ferencvaros lessons and responsibility to win consistently

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim knows that results are needed in Europe, but once again stressed that he foresees a ‘long-term project’.

Milan have racked up just three out of 12 points in the first half of the league phase, meaning they really need to change gear if they are to progress into the next round. Tonight’s game is another very tough one on paper, given Olympiacos have 10 points on the board and are in the top eight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim has named a strong starting line-up featuring the likes of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos and the top scorer Alphadjo Cisse. However, what doesn’t help the cause at all are the nine injury absentees, which is noticeable when looking at the bench.

The head coach spoke to Sky in the build-up to kick-off in Greece to shed light on his selections and the importance of learning lessons in Europe. MilanNews relayed his words.

You’ve gone with an attacking side tonight…

“In football, you have to defend and attack. We have to defend with 11 men and attack with 11 men. The players know what positions they have to occupy and are ready.

“We have to be more compact, and even with these attacking players on the pitch, we can defend better than in other Europa League matches.”

Did the players learn their lesson after Ferencvaros?

“I think they understand. We’ve seen videos, we’re working. Against Ferencvaros, we were sluggish because we weren’t compact and focused on the details. In Europe, we need to raise our game and do what we’ve done several times in Serie A.”

Are you ready to prove you can play three good games in a row in a week?

“I think we have to be a great team. To be that, you have to win both in Serie A and in Europe. We have that responsibility. Results matter a lot, obviously, but we’re on a long-term project. We need to understand if we can play during the week, and today will be an additional test.”
