Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1610. This is going to hurt: Liverpool reportedly preparing for massive departure

Liverpool are preparing for a massive departure that will change the side dramatically. This one is going to hurt.

Liverpool have said goodbye to a series of legends over the last few years. It really started in 2021 when Gini Wijnaldum left for Paris Saint-Germain and then Sadio Mane decided to leave for Bayern Munich a year later. Slowly but surely, Jürgen Klopp's team has disappeared.

Jordan Henderson, Roberto Firmino and Fabinho left in 2023. Klopp himself left in 2024, as did Joel Matip and Thiago. 2025 was a big one - Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid. Then things got even more heartbreaking in 2026 as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate departed.

Salah's exit was arguably the most difficult of the lot. That was the biggest sign that things had moved on - the icon of Klopp's team deciding it was time to leave.

And now 2027 awaits and things are set to continue down the same path. The final stars of that great side have expiring contracts and it increasingly looks like it's time to say goodbye.

Liverpool are reportedly preparing the exit of Alisson Becker, whose contract will expire at the end of the campaign. Alisson's deal was due to end in 2026 but the Reds triggered an option to extend it by a year.

Juventus did try to get a deal done last summer regardless of that, offering a minimal fee to Liverpool. Nothing came of it, however, as no one at the Reds seemed keen to sell the Brazilian.

But Alisson may leave next year. Liverpool won't want him to go but offering a new contract to a goalkeeper with his injury history feels like a big risk. A risk they may not want to take if other options are available.

Of course, 'other options' of Alisson's calibre are few and far between. L'Equipe, though, understand that Liverpool have found one. They're eyeing Robin Risser of RC Lens, who was voted the best in Ligue 1 last season.

The 21-year-old is being discussed at Anfield internally as a potential option should Alisson leave. It's the first real sign we've had that the club are very much open to moving on from arguably their greatest-ever goalkeeper.

But we wonder if that could change because of Risser. There's intense competition for him and if he picks somewhere else, we imagine Liverpool will 'settle' for renewing Alisson's deal.

It's very much wait and see, then, but the Reds are certainly preparing for Alisson's exit.

#1607. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1605. 'That's their problem' – Jose Mourinho sends clear message to Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 16:17

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior are subject to the same selection criteria as the rest of his squad, warning that any dissatisfaction with being named on the bench is a matter for the players themselves.

The Portuguese manager was questioned about the status of his attacking stars during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's La Liga encounter with Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid's recent improvement has coincided with Bellingham's excellent form and a resurgence from Vinicius, who has faced increased competition for his place following the summer arrival of Yan Diomande. Mourinho, however, believes that the collective spirit he has established since returning to the Spanish capital is helping him manage those individual ambitions.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho dismissed the suggestion that certain members of his squad enjoy preferential treatment.

"If one day they are on the bench and they don't like it, that's their problem," said the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager, who stressed that Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius were on an equal footing with their teammates.

Mourinho acknowledged that Mbappe has yet to start a match on the bench this season, while Bellingham has only done so once. He explained that the difference in playing time between the pair and other members of the squad was justified by their performances.

Mbappe has registered 19 goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, while Bellingham demonstrated his importance to the team once again in Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Madrid were trailing at half time when Mourinho introduced the England international, who subsequently scored a superb goal and provided the assist for Vinicius to complete the scoring.

Such performances help explain why Mourinho has been reluctant to rest either player. The Portuguese nevertheless insisted that the team's objectives take precedence over individual ambitions and expressed satisfaction at how his players have accepted that principle.

The debate surrounding Madrid's attacking options has intensified in recent weeks, with Vinicius returning to form after a difficult start to the campaign and a four-match La Liga suspension.

The Brazilian made an important contribution from the bench in last weekend's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo before finding the net against PSV, giving Mourinho another selection decision to make ahead of the Alaves fixture.

However, Mourinho rejected the idea that Vinicius and Diomande should be regarded as rivals, explaining that both players share the same objectives and that the Brazilian has retained the support of his teammates throughout his difficult spell.

The Madrid boss also dismissed concerns about the atmosphere within the dressing room, revealing that he has not encountered any significant problems during his first five months back at the club.

His satisfaction with the current squad extends to his plans for the January transfer window, with Mourinho making it clear that he would prefer to finish the season with the players already at his disposal.

"I don't want anyone to leave either; the door is closed," the Portuguese explained after ruling out the need for new signings.

That stance is particularly noteworthy given the limited opportunities afforded to some of Madrid's younger attacking players. With Rodrygo also working his way back from a long-term injury, competition for places could become even greater during the second half of the campaign.

Mourinho's comments suggest that he would rather manage that competition internally than reduce his attacking options midway through a season in which Madrid are competing for honours on several fronts.

#1602. Manchester United Plan 20 Million Pound Bid For Bundesliga Defender

Home » Home 2 » Manchester United Plan 20 Million Pound Bid For Bundesliga Defender

Louis van Gaal’s hand may be forced into making a transfer this January, after injury woes continue to adversely effect the Red Devils. And it looks like he’s set to raid none other than the Bundesliga club that dumped them out of the UEFA Champions League.

23-year-old fullback Ricardo Rodriguez has caught the eye of the Manchester United officials, with The Sun reporting that the club have sent scouts to watch him twice already and that he is very high on manager Louis van Gaal’s transfer wish list.

The Swiss defender is valued int he region of 20 million pounds, but has a release clause of 27 million pounds at German club Vfl Wolfsburg, where he has spent the past 4 years. This means that Manchester United will have to negotiate quite a bit to land the player without breaking the bank yet again. They will also have to be wary of Real Madrid, who are also reportedly interested.

Italian right back Matteo Darmian came off with an injury in the second half of United’s 1-0 loss to Southampton, he is the latest in the list of injured defenders at the club. Phil Jones, Ashley Young, Luke Shaw, Marcos Rojo and Antonio Valencia are all members of the walking wounded at Old Trafford.

This means that buying a fullback is a top priority for the club this January and we could well see a bug bid launched by the Red Devils for the highly rated Rodriguez.

#1601. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1600. Opinion: Liverpool will sign perfect player for Andoni Iraola, he'll only cost £19m

Andoni Iraola has done a pretty decent job since being appointed as Liverpool's manager.

He's managed to get his team to fourth in the Premier League table with only seven points separating them from first-placed Arsenal.

Obviously, this is still a decent number of points to chip away at but, if the Gunners continue dropping points by drawing games against teams such as Newcastle, the Reds could find themselves back in the title race soon.

Nobody knows what lies ahead for any team but, if Liverpool manage to pull off even half of the transfers they've been linked with, they'll be storming their way up the table.

And to make things even sweeter, the perfect signing for Iraola has just emerged.

Arhcie Brown has a £19.2 million release clause in his contract

So many areas among Liverpool's ranks still need upgrading.

This is a horrible thing to write as, across the last couple of years, well over £600 million has been spent on new players by the Reds.

Some of the transfers that they've made have worked out for the better but, others haven't quite hit the mark.

Milos Kerkez is an example of this because, even though he has had a fair few decent performances, his inconsistency is terrible.

Some days he can be seen as the Premier League's best left-back and, on others, he could end up being the worst player on the pitch.

This has forced fans to ask for a new left-back with Florian Plettenberg now sharing a rather intriguing update on Liverpool target, Archie Brown.

"Archie Brown has a release clause worth around €23m, valid for both the winter and summer transfer windows. The 23 y/o is a regular starter at Fenerbahçe and has also impressed with some very strong performances in the Champions League," he wrote.

"Under contract until 2028, a move is planned, with Premier League clubs already making enquiries."

Archie Brown would fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans

Not only would Brown be classed as homegrown but, he'd also be one of the cheapest transfers on the market.

Recent links with Liverpool and Alejandro Balde have emerged with Barcelona demanding close to €50 million for the Spaniard.

Others such as Daniel Svensson have also been linked with a move but, again, Borussia Dortmund want over €40 million for him.

Each of these players would be exceptional additions but, Brown for €23 million (£19 million) is a deal that's too good to pass up.

He put in the performance of a lifetime when Liverpool faced Fenerbahce earlier in the season and, if he can replicate that form in the Premier League, the Reds would be onto a winner.

Liverpool signing Brown would also give Kerkez a genuine challenger for his position which might even help him develop his performance.

Since the price for Brown is so good, Liverpool will have to act fast and get straight on with securing his services when the January transfer window opens up, otherwise, they'll end up kicking themselves for missing out on it.

#1599. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1598. Como vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 16:43, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 16:48

Midweek winners in Europe, Como and Juventus will resume their pursuit of Serie A's top four when they clash at Stadio Sinigaglia on Sunday.

Both teams are on track to qualify directly for the last 16 in their continental campaigns, but they currently trail Italy's top quartet.

Ascending to third place in the Champions League table - above the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona - Como continued their incredible European exploits on Tuesday evening, with a 1-0 home win over AEK Athens.

The little Lombardy club are firmly on course to reach the knockout phase on their continental debut, and they are still in an open Serie A title race.   Though they recently lost to Inter Milan once again, normal service was resumed last weekend, when Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Sinigaglia.

Victory kept them in touch with both Milan sides and the two unbeaten Rome clubs, and the Lariani have claimed a club record 26 points from their first 12 top-flight fixtures.

Unbeaten as hosts this season, Cesc Fabregas has seen his team concede just one goal in five home games, including four consecutive clean sheets - against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia and Cagliari.

Como now face a crucial clash in the fight for Champions League qualification, and success on Sunday would open up an eight-point lead over Juventus.

Before doing the double over Juve last season, they had not beaten the Turin giants at home since 1952, but a pair of 2-0 wins helped them sneak past the Bianconeri to claim fourth place in the end.

Reflecting their sudden change in status, Juventus have never before faced Como while trailing in the Serie A standings, yet that is now the situation they face.

While the Lariani were dining at Europe’s top table, Juve extended their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League in midweek, defeating Omonia 4-1 in Turin.

Posing a potential solution to their striker problems, Jeff Ekhator found the net on his first start for the club, and across all competitions the Bianconeri have scored 14 goals across their last five games.

In Europe, Juventus are set to cruise through as one of the top eight finishers - having claimed 13 points from a possible 15 so far - but it has been a more mixed picture on the domestic scene.

Despite thumping Venezia 4-0 last week, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit squad lag 11 points behind league leaders Lazio in sixth place, partly due to their sub-par away form.

Juve’s Serie A record on the road is two wins, two draws and two defeats - with eight goals scored and eight conceded - so visiting Como will surely cause some concern.

Como are still missing ex-Juventus striker Moise Kean, plus Willy Kambwala and Jesus Rodriguez, but Fabregas could have two wingers back from injury this weekend.

Jayden Addai and Assane Diao both face fitness tests, while midfielder Maxence Caqueret is a strong doubt.

Without Kean, Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the Lariani’s front line, having scored 11 goals in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Juve’s top Serie A scorer is Brazilian centre-back Bremer with a modest three goals, though Nick Woltemade has been directly involved in three across his last two league games and is faring well in the Europa League.

The German striker must compete with Ekhator and Randal Kolo Muani to start at the Sinigaglia, where Spalletti will be without several key men.

Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined, while Nico Gonzalez remains a doubt; more positively, Kerim Alajbegovic and Pierre Kalulu could both be named on the bench.

Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, McKennie, Kolo Muani; Woltemade

Two of Italy's tightest defences will face off on Sunday night: since Spalletti's arrival in Turin last November, Juventus have kept 19 clean sheets and Como have 20.

While the hosts have been far more convincing, Juve are putting together a good run of results and their long absence list is starting to clear.

#1597. Player Ratings: Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan – Hutchinson unplayable; Pulisic class

AC Milan completed a crucial comeback as they scored four goals against Olympiacos in the second half. One man in particular was behind the Rossoneri’s resurgence and below are the player ratings.

49 minutes into the game, it looked like Ruben Amorim and his men were heading for another disappointing defeat in the Europa League. Then, Omari Hutchinson decided enough was enough and inspired his teammates to a massive comeback.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Hutchinson (9.5 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

👎 De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

👔 Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

Maignan (6): He made a great save in the first half to deny Martins. Some have suggested that he could have come out to parry the corner away on the first goal, but I don’t entirely agree. Anyway, he couldn’t do much about the second goal and was okay with his feet.

Gila (7): He was his usual aggressive self and that helped Milan on several occasions. Perhaps more so than his ability to win the ball back, however, it was his clearances that meant the most as he stopped some very good crosses. He also had a great overlapping run before the Rossoneri’s second goal.

De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

Diawara (5): Touch and judgment. Those are the two things that let him down tonight. He put himself in too many tough positions due to the touch, and his judgment didn’t help when it came to anticipating the passes over the top. Just a really poor display, sadly.

Estupinan (5.5): He wasn’t terrible, but not good either. A rather quiet performance from him when you think about it, so it wasn’t enough for a pass here.

Jashari (6): It was a good opportunity for him and he sort of took it, I guess? It was very much a decent display overall. He had that great pass for Cisse that nearly led to a goal and also helped well in the build-up. However, he had a few misplaced passes and perhaps could have done more to stop Pirola in his tracks before the first goal.

Rabiot (6): In fairness to him, he did have a couple of important clearances defensively but in attack, he definitely didn’t add as much as we have seen in recent weeks. The goal contributions streak had to come to an end at some point. Still, overall, it was an okay performance.

Moreira (7): The goal obviously helps his rating a lot, especially since he remained composed, but he also had a couple of really nice switches to Hutchinson on the other side. He was a tad wasteful in some situations, in my opinion, but a decent display plus a goal deserves a good rating.

Hutchinson (9.5 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

Cisse (7.5): Another goal for the youngster! I thought he did well at left-wing, nearly scoring that goal despite the goalkeeper’s challenge, but he continued to do well at centre-forward. The movement and header on the goal proved once again that he’s got it.

Ramos (5.5): Similarly to Estupinan, as both were taken off at half-time, it was more a quiet performance than it was a really bad one. That said, the No.9 had a couple of moments on the counter that could have been handled better.

Musah (6.5): It’s hard to put my finger on exactly what he changed, but he brought something to the game which helped Milan play better. Could absolutely be his movement as he covered a lot of ground and wasn’t afraid to drive forward either.

Pulisic (8.5): World class is probably the best way to describe him. You could immediately see the difference he was going to make, although perhaps no one predicted that goal. It was a tremendous strike to complete the turnaround for Milan. Tremendous! And then he got the assist for Moreira. We can forgive the miss just before that.

Tomori (6.5): Almost a 7 for him, but it’s possible that I might be influenced by just how poor De Winter and Diawara were. Anyway, the Englishman returned with a strong performance and showed that he’s one to rely on.

Terracciano (6): He’s the master of always opting for the easy way out, but in this case, that was probably exactly what Milan needed.

Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

🚨Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil on AC Milan’s 15-minute comeback against Olympiacos:

We lost today because we failed to do our assignment on Omari Hutchinson.

We initially had a plan to contain him and keep him quiet. We wanted to stop him receiving the ball facing our defenders, because once he turns and starts running at you, the problem becomes much bigger.

And for most of the first half, we did it.

Even in the second half, for some time, we managed it.

Hutchinson started taking responsibility.

And suddenly our defensive structure was changing because everybody was worried about him.

We actually removed two players from marking him because we wanted to protect the space around him.

He got the better of Onyemachi, scored the first goal and suddenly Milan believed again.

I was angry with my players because we allowed him to get into those situations.

When you are 2–0 up at home against AC Milan, you cannot allow one player to turn the entire match around.

There is very little you can do when you have a winger running at you with that much confidence.

He is small, he is close to the ground, his balance is excellent and he changes direction very quickly.

That makes him extremely difficult to defend.

If you go to ground, you risk catching his leg instead of the ball and getting a yellow card.

If you don’t go to ground, he pushes the ball past you and runs.

So the defender has to make a decision in one second.

Our defenders decided to give him the space.

And once he realised they were backing away from him, he became even more confident.

That is when you know you have a problem.

Because a winger like that doesn’t need five chances.

Give him one successful dribble and suddenly he believes he can beat everybody.

We went from controlling the game to defending like we were frightened of one player.

We should have made somebody stay close to him instead of allowing him to receive the ball and face our defence.

But football punishes you when you hesitate.

We went from a perfect win to a perfect defeat in fifteen minutes.

Because I don’t think we were the worse team.

I don’t think our football suddenly disappeared.

We simply failed to deal with one player when the game became chaotic.

I told him, ‘You have a very good player there.’

Because if Hutchinson learns how to control games like that consistently, not just moments, then Milan have something very special.

And unfortunately for us, we allowed him to do it.”

Other highest marks for me go to Cisse and Moreira, but neither was above a 7.5.

Cisse – Great header and great nose for goal, ties up the match, but he really needs to improve his vision and passing and dial down the selfishness a bit. His goal was great, but his next two touches should have been passes, but he tried ridiculous shots. 7.0

Moreira – Tons of energy and grinta and just a player I like a lot, but he was also sloppy at times in this game. Awful set piece attempt. Should have passed more quickly in several instances. Nice goal on the last kick of the game. 7.5

Maingan – I too think he should have come out for the corner kick. And then it’s an own goal off his back. The saves weren’t terribly difficult nor was his play with his feet good enough to redeem him. Key player for us, but this was not his best. 5.5

Jashari – I like this player and was really ready to love this performance, but at the end of the day it was average at best. A bit anonymous. He made several great passes but also made far too many sideways and backwards moves. Maybe we’re spoiled by Modric’s amazing inimitable style, but Jashari just doesn’t seem ambitious enough. He might still develop, I’m not sure, let’s try him a few more times, but this was not the big show we wanted to see. 6.0

Gila — solid on the ball and some great clearances, too aggressive at times. He does raise the level of our defense overall, and made some good one v one stops. 6.5

Koni — Poor, but I’m not quite as low on his game as others. Yes, the second goal was on him, but it wasn’t an awful giveaway, just a long ball that wasn’t hit hard or high enough, and the opponent made a great header to intercept it and place it into a teammate’s path. Koni did make some great interceptions. 5.5

Diawara – Not good enough on the ball and got beat several times. I like how this player is developing, but he was not great today. 5.5.

Estupinan – Poor passing, little energy going forward, but didn’t get beat too badly. I’m ready to move on from this guy. 5.0

Rabiot – Not one of his vintage matches, but not awful. He is such a classy player that even subpar performances from him are decent. 6.0

Ramos – I just don’t see the longterm path here for this guy. We paid a lot for him, and he does some good things, but he’s actually not great on the ball. He can’t hold it up, and he is sometimes sloppy with even unpressured possession. I’d like to see Cisse start every other match for the next month, and see how that goes. 5.0

In addition to Puli, I think Musah and Tomori were both huge positive difference makers. Amorim making good subs and good adjustments.

Musah adds a lot in termis of physicality and energy in the midfield, and he won the ball that lead to Puli’s winner. 7.0

Tomori brought great energy and concentration and I’d like to see more of him. 7.0.

Terracciano – This guy is simply not at the level and should be sold asap. I’ve been saying it since day one. He scares me and always looks about to give the ball away. He doesn’t have the skill on the ball to simply make a dummy or pause a pass, as we saw when he was in the corner and panicked and played the ball off of Moreira instead of the simple pass to Jashari. Luckily in this game, this didn’t hurt us, and he actually didn’t get beat. 5.0

Commotto – barely touched the ball, seemed shy and overawed. In one moment he could have taken the ball upfield but was too tentative. Could be a great player that just needs more time, but for this match he made no positive contributions and slightly hurt us. 5.0

And Amorim outcoached our opponents by making great adjustments at halftime and gambled a bit by taking Ramos and Estu off at halftime. 7.5

#1596. Aston Villa vs Chelsea FC: Possible Lineups, Stats, Prediction & Odds | English Premier League

Home » Home 2 » Aston Villa vs Chelsea FC: Possible Lineups, Stats, Prediction & Odds | English Premier League

Aston Villa will play their first Premier League game since the departure of manager Remi Garde by mutual consent earlier in the week. Assistant manager Eric Black has taken over the reins at Villa Park and the Scot will look to salvage whatever he can from this season, with his side needing a miracle to avoid relegation. It is understood that Black is to stay caretaker manager till the end of the season or until Villa are able to appoint a new full-time manager.

Chelsea will see the likes of Willian, Cesc Fabregas, Pedro and Gary Cahill among others returning from international duty and will look to hit the ground running following the break.

Since taking over from Jose Mourinho, Guus Hiddink has been able to to provide some much needed stability to what looked like a fast sinking Chelsea ship. However, the Blues sit 10th in the league table, with European competition looking increasingly unlikely next season. As such, Chelsea supporters have been clamouring for the likes of Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Kenedy and Bertrand Traore to get more game time for the rest of the campaign.

Possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Guzan; Hutton, Clark, Cissokho, Lescott; Westwood, Guey; Gil, Veretout, Ayew; Gestede

Possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Terry, Cahill, Ivanovic, Azpilicueta; Mikel, Fabregas; Oscar, Willian, Pedro; Remy

Aston Villa 1 – 3 Chelsea It should be a comfortable victory for Chelsea if they were to play to their potential and with some endeavour — something that hasn’t been seen too often from the West London outfit this season. Nothing but victory should suffice for Chelsea but with the way things have gone this season, it wouldn’t be too surprising if Villa came away with something from this tie.

#1595. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1594. Opinion: Julian Ward will be forced to change Liverpool's transfer plans

Julian Ward has a lot of decisions to make ahead of his first transfer window as Liverpool's new sporting director.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes as the Reds' new director after Hughes chose to seek pastures new and join Al-Hilal.

Hughes has spent the most money of any Liverpool sporting director ever and, the Reds still need to add more new players to their ranks.

It's unclear whether this is because of all the changes at Anfield or if it's because of another reason.

But, if Ward thought his job was going to be easy, he can think again as he may already be forced to change his winter transfer plans.

Victor Munoz's injury could massively hurt Liverpool

Liverpool's attack was one of the main areas that they focused on improving this summer.

Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were brought in for a combined total worth over £150 million.

And, while both players have had their moments, it still feels like Liverpool could do with adding another player or two to their ranks.

But, since there are also many other areas among their first-team squad that also need changing, it didn't really feel like any deals for attackers were going to occur in January.

However, Munoz was unfortunately forced off the pitch during the Reds' 3-0 win against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

So, depending on how long he's out for, the Reds may need to turn their transfer plans upside down and add another attacker to their ranks.

Liverpool will be hoping that Victor Munoz isn't out for too long

Recently, Munoz has been finding his feet at Anfield.

The attacker was clearly brought in during the summer transfer window to be a back-up.

He only cost the club around £35 million which, in this day and age, is a steal.

His initial performances weren't all that great but, over the last couple of weeks, he's got himself into a purple patch of form with his blistering pace being one of his best assets.

In addition to this, Munoz is only 23 years old so, he still has a lot of his career ahead of him which means that he's probably going to get better.

So, a long-term injury is definitely not what he needs right now.

Nobody knows exactly what has happened to the Spaniard yet but, the Reds will certainly be hoping that it's nothing too serious.

#1592. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc

🗣️"Szoboszlai scores A LOT OF BANGERS"😂Needless to say Cody Gakpo was really impressed with Dominik Szoboszlai's goal for Liverpool 👏#ITVFootball | @LFC | @Carabao_Cup | @gabrielclarke05 pic.twitter.com/O3bs6Y9M2p

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye

He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Just one player remains from Liverpool’s starting XI against Fulham on Saturday and that is Ronald Araujo. Virgil van Dijk and Florian Wirtz are given the night off for the home side.

Roberto De Zerbi makes eight changes from Tottenham’s draw against Everton, with Archie Gray, Rodrigo Bentancur and Omar Marmoush the three players to remain in the starting XI.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

#1590. Opinion: Liverpool will sign the next Ronald Araujo for €35m

Ronald Araujo's Liverpool future is still up in the air.

The defender has been top class for the Reds since he joined them in the summer and, although it took him a couple of games to get into Iraola's plans, he's now earned himself a guaranteed place in his starting XI.

Indeed, he is being used as a right-back which isn't his natural position but, he's that good in both positions that it doesn't really matter where he's played.

He helps bring an extra layer of defensive stability to Anfield and he's also helped shore up their back line massively.

This has allowed Jeremy Jacquet the time to adjust to Premier League life and has ensured that he was one of the best defensive transfers made in the summer.

But, since Liverpool's option to buy the midfielder is rather high at €55 million, alternative options are now making their way onto the Reds' shortlist.

Liverpool can sign Mohamed Simakan for €35 million

Right-back has been a problem area for Liverpool ever since they got rid of Trent Alexander-Arnold last summer.

Jeremie Frimpong was brought in to try and help plug the gap while Conor Bradley was expected to take over as Liverpool's first choice right-back.

But, thanks to the injuries that both players suffered, the Reds' plans didn't work out exactly as they wanted them to which resulted in Araujo being signed this summer.

As mentioned, the Uruguayan has been in fine form this term but, since he's not an actual Liverpool player, a decision needs to be made on his future.

But, with the way that things seem to be going, Araujo looks likely to return to Barcelona.

This has led to fans asking many questions about who their starting right-back is going to be with Caught Offside now throwing a new defender into the mix.

"Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Newcastle have all continued scouting Simakan, although no formal offers or advanced negotiations have taken place," they wrote.

"For Liverpool, Simakan’s versatility is particularly attractive.

"With long-term succession planning required in central defence, signing a player capable of operating centrally while also covering right-back would give the squad valuable flexibility.

"The asking price will be crucial. At €35m-€40m, Simakan would represent a relatively manageable investment compared with some of the €70m-plus defenders currently being linked with both clubs.

"There are still questions about adapting back to European football after his spell in Saudi Arabia, but at 26 he should be entering his peak years."

Mohamed Simakan can cover all the positions Ronald Araujo does for Liverpool

Not only is Mohamed Simakan younger than Araujo but, he's also worth a lot less.

€35 million for a 26-year-old in this market is unheard of, especially for a versatile defender such as the Frenchman.

As Caught Offside mention, his last couple of years being spent in Saudi Arabia do pose a bit of a worry but, within a few months of making a return to European football, he should be able to get back to his best.

The main stumbling block between Liverpool and Barcelona for an Araujo deal is the fee that the La Liga outfit want.

So, the fact that Simakan is younger, can play in all the positions that Araujo covers for Liverpool and the fact that he'd be cheaper for them to buy, makes a deal for the Frenchman a no-brainer.
